Name: Box Hill main car park (National Trust)
Address: Box Hill summit, off Zig Zag Road / Box Hill Road, Tadworth KT20 7LB (NT address)
Description: The classic start for Box Hill: park at the summit and you're only a couple of minutes from the famous view over Dorking towards the South Downs. Expect it to be busy on sunny weekends.
Practical: NT members park free; others pay by machine or JustPark app (£2 up to 1 hr, £4 up to 2 hrs, £6 up to 4 hrs, £9 all day). No phone signal, so set the app up before you go. No overnight parking or camping. Café, servery and toilets next to the car park (toilets open when the café or servery is open); Blue Badge spaces; consolidated gravel surface. NT says the main and east car parks together have over 200 spaces.
Nearby: Salomons Memorial viewpoint (about 150 m). Box Hill Fort, the 1890s 'Old Fort' (about 200 m). Major Peter Labelliere's Grave, where local lore says his ghost still roams (about 250 m). Woodland paths lead down to the Box Hill Stepping Stones and the GHQ Line Pillboxes (about 0.5 mile, steep, with around 270 steps), then The Stepping Stones pub in Westhumble and the Burford Bridge Hotel (about 1 mile on foot). Juniper Top and Broadwood's Folly are about 1 mile away.
Coord_Source: OSM way 427571289 (amenity=parking, NT ref 8503), polygon centroid
Notes: Tier Main: NT visitor hub with café, servery, toilets and over 200 spaces (shared with the East car park, per NT). Largest public car park on Box Hill in OSM (about 6,900 m²).

Name: Box Hill East car park (National Trust)
Address: Box Hill Road, Box Hill summit, Tadworth (east of the visitor centre)
Description: The National Trust's second summit car park, a short stroll east of the café and viewpoint. It's the only one on the hill suitable for coaches, and the 21 bus turns round here.
Practical: NT members park free; others pay by machine or JustPark app (£2 up to 1 hr, £4 up to 2 hrs, £6 up to 4 hrs, £9 all day). No phone signal, so set the app up before you go. No overnight parking or camping. Uneven gravel surface. Café, servery and toilets are at the visitor centre a short walk west. Large vehicles should approach via Box Hill village, not Zig Zag Road.
Nearby: Salomons Memorial viewpoint (about 0.2 mile). Box Hill Fort (about 0.3 mile). Major Peter Labelliere's Grave (about 0.35 mile). Broadwood's Folly on Lodge Hill and the open chalk slopes of Juniper Top are about 0.75 mile away. The Stepping Stones and the River Mole are about 0.6 mile away as the crow flies, down a steep descent.
Coord_Source: OSM way 32492198 (amenity=parking, name 'East Car Park'), polygon centroid
Notes: CORRECTION: William's file wondered whether this exists. It does. NT names an 'east car park' at the summit, suitable for coaches and with the bus turning area. Tier Main because it's part of the NT's 200+ space summit parking, with coach access and the bus stop. OSM area alone is about 1,900 m².

Name: Polesden Lacey car park (National Trust)
Address: Polesden Lacey, Great Bookham, near Dorking RH5 6BD
Description: A big, well-run car park for the Edwardian house and its 1,600-acre estate. It's a good base for the gardens or for longer walks south towards Ranmore Common.
Practical: NT members park free (scan your physical card at the machine); non-members £5 all day, by cash at the machine, card at Visitor Reception, or JustPark (location code 80650). Car park open 07:30–18:00 on 21 Nov 2026; hours vary by season. Main toilet block by the car park, plus a coffee shop, café and shop. Ten EV charging points; Blue Badge parking; gravel surface.
Nearby: Polesden Lacey house and gardens (about 300 m; admission charged, NT members free). Estate parkland and woodland trails start from the car park. Ranmore Common woods are about 1 mile south, and St Barnabas Church, Ranmore about 1.5 miles. The NT describes a 1.5-mile cross-country walk to Ranmore Common and on to Denbies Hillside.
Notes: Tier Main: largest car park on the list (OSM about 11,200 m²), with toilets, café and shop. Charge confirmed on the NT page (£5/day for non-members, not the Box Hill tariff).

Name: Headley Heath main car park (National Trust)
Address: Headley Common Road (B2033), Headley KT18 6NN (NT address)
Description: A big open-air start for Headley Heath's tangle of tracks across heather, woodland and chalk downland. It feels wilder and quieter than nearby Box Hill.
Practical: NT members park free; others pay by machine or JustPark app (£2 up to 1 hr, £4 up to 2 hrs, £6 up to 4 hrs, £9 all day). No phone signal, so set the app up before you go. No overnight parking or camping. JustPark location code 80589 (you can pay up to 48 hrs after your visit). A mobile drinks and snacks van (not NT) usually parks here, 9am–4.30pm. No toilets. Recycled asphalt / fine gravel surface.
Nearby: Headley Heath's open heath, woods and chalk slopes (a Site of Special Scientific Interest) start at the car park edge. Belted Galloway cattle graze parts of the heath, so keep dogs close. The second NT car park, Brimmer, is about 0.4 mile south. The NT suggests a long circular footpath walk linking Headley Heath with Box Hill (about 5 hours).
Coord_Source: OSM way 24974949 (amenity=parking, 'Headley Heath Main Car Park', NT), polygon centroid
Notes: Tier Main: NT main car park (as named by the NT), about 3,700 m² in OSM, with a refreshment van. Charge confirmed: pay and display, NT members free.

Name: Denbies Wine Estate visitor car park
Address: Denbies Wine Estate, London Road (A24), Dorking RH5 6AA
Description: England's best-known vineyard sits right on the edge of town, with miles of public footpaths climbing through the vines. It makes an easy start with a coffee or a glass at the end.
Practical: Free parking for estate visitors. This is private, not a public car park, so be a customer if you start a walk here. Eight Blue Badge spaces near the entrance. Toilets, restaurant and café in the visitor centre during opening hours. Dogs on leads where asked.
Nearby: Public footpaths through the vineyard (the estate says about seven miles of them). Village Greens Farm Shop at Denbies, Surrey Hills Brewery and Dorking Distillery are all on site. Across the A24, the Box Hill Stepping Stones and The Stepping Stones pub in Westhumble are about 0.5–0.75 mile on foot, and Westhumble Chapel and the Burford Bridge Hotel about 0.75 mile. Dorking town centre is about 1 mile away.
Notes: Tier Main: about 9,800 m² in OSM, with toilets, café and restaurant. Private estate parking for visitors; kept on the map because it's a genuine, well-used walk start, with a clear 'be a customer' caveat.

Name: Denbies Hillside car park, Ranmore (Ranmore East)
Address: Ranmore Common Road, near Dorking RH5 6SR (NT address)
Description: The first National Trust car park you reach at the top of Ranmore Common Road, and the bigger of the two at Ranmore. Step out onto chalk downland with one of the best views in Surrey, across the Dorking valley towards Box Hill and Leith Hill.
Practical: NT members park free; others pay by machine or JustPark app (£2 up to 1 hr, £4 up to 2 hrs, £6 up to 4 hrs, £9 all day). No phone signal, so set the app up before you go. No overnight parking or camping. JustPark location ID 80557. Level parking, loose compacted gravel. No toilets (nearest in Westcott village). Dog bins just outside the car park.
Nearby: Denbies Hillside viewpoint (about 100 m), on chalk grassland known for Adonis blue and chalkhill blue butterflies. St Barnabas Church, Ranmore, the 'church on the North Downs Way', is about 0.3 mile away. Ranmore Common woods are just across the road. Second World War pillboxes line the North Downs Way to the west, and The Prince of Wales in Westcott is about 1.25 miles away (the NT says about 35 minutes on foot from Westcott).
Coord_Source: OSM relation 6802958 (amenity=parking, 'Denbies Hillside', NT), outer-ring centroid
Notes: CORRECTION: this is William's 'Ranmore Common East', listed as small. The NT calls it Denbies Hillside car park. It's bigger than Ranmore West (OSM about 2,000 m² against 775 m²) and it's the NT's headline paid car park here, so it moves up to Main.

Name: Starveall Corner car park, Leith Hill
Address: Leith Hill Road, Wotton RH5 6LX (Surrey County Council postcode)
Description: The largest of the free Leith Hill car parks, and the gentlest way up to the tower. It's also where Surrey County Council's waymarked Acorn and Nightjar trails begin.
Practical: Free (Surrey County Council, on Wotton Estate land). Unmarked spaces; 1.9 m height barrier. No toilets. Dog bin nearby. Kiosk at the base of Leith Hill Tower. Toilets only at Leith Hill Place when the house is open.
Nearby: Leith Hill Tower, the highest point in south-east England (about 0.75 mile; the NT calls it easy walking). Leith Hill Rhododendron Wood (about 0.3 mile). Leith Hill Place and Darwin's Worm Stone (about 0.6 mile as the crow flies). The heathland of Duke's Warren is about 0.9 mile away. SCC's Acorn trail (2.6 miles) and Nightjar trail (3.5 miles) both start here.
Coord_Source: OSM way 724310934 (amenity=parking, 'Starveall Corner Car Park'), polygon centroid
Notes: CORRECTION: it's not NT and not permit-only. SCC lists it as free, on Wotton Estate land. It's also not the closest car park to the tower: the NT gives ¾ mile from Starveall, ¼ mile from Windy Gap. Tier Main as the biggest Leith Hill car park (OSM about 2,800 m²) and the trailhead for SCC's two waymarked trails.

Name: Shere village car park
Address: Entrance off Upper Street / London Lane, Shere GU5 9HE
Description: The official car park for one of Surrey's prettiest villages, right in the centre. It suits a pub lunch, the church and a loop out into the Tillingbourne valley.
Practical: About 90 spaces (Shere Parish Council). First 30 minutes free, then £1 an hour, 9am–6pm daily, payable via RingGo (pay up to 24 hrs later). what3words ///page.forks.icon (published by the parish council). The council asks visitors not to park in the village lanes.
Nearby: The White Horse and The Bray in Shere (both about 250 m). St James Church, Shere, with its medieval anchoress's cell (about 200 m). Netley Park woods and their Type 24 Pillbox are about 0.75 mile away, and St Peter and St Paul (Old Saxon Church), Albury about 0.75 mile. Silent Pool and Silent Pool Distillery are about 1 mile.
Coord_Source: OSM way 40444642 (amenity=parking), polygon centroid; matches Shere Parish Council location
Notes: CORRECTION: it was listed as small with 20 spaces. The parish council publishes about 90 spaces, which makes it Main. It is a charged car park (Ocean Parking).

Name: Windy Gap car park, Leith Hill
Address: Abinger Road, near Coldharbour RH5 6HG (Surrey County Council postcode)
Description: A small roadside car park that is the closest to Leith Hill Tower. The catch is a steep flight of uneven steps.
Practical: Free (Surrey County Council, on Wotton Estate land). Unmarked spaces; 1.9 m height barrier. No toilets. Not suitable for wheelchairs or buggies (long flight of steps). Kiosk at the base of the tower.
Nearby: Leith Hill Tower (about ¼ mile up steep steps, per the NT). Leith Hill Place, Darwin's Worm Stone and Leith Hill Rhododendron Wood are about 0.5 mile away as the crow flies. Duke's Warren heath and Christ Church, Coldharbour are about 0.75 mile, and The Plough Inn in Coldharbour about 1 mile.
Notes: CORRECTION: it's SCC-managed and free, not NT. It's the closest car park to the tower. Tier Small: mapped only as a point in OSM, with no official capacity and no facilities. William listed it with 30 spaces; no official count is published.

Name: Landslip car park, Leith Hill (National Trust)
Description: A National Trust car park on the eastern flank of Leith Hill, handy for Coldharbour and a stiff climb to the tower.
Practical: NT members park free; others pay by machine or JustPark app (£2 up to 1 hr, £4 up to 2 hrs, £6 up to 4 hrs, £9 all day). No phone signal, so set the app up before you go. No overnight parking or camping. JustPark location code 80601. Compacted surface. No toilets.
Nearby: Christ Church, Coldharbour (about 0.3 mile). The Plough Inn in Coldharbour (about 0.75 mile on foot). Leith Hill Tower (about ¾ mile on a steep gradient, per the NT). Duke's Warren heathland is about 0.6 mile away.
Coord_Source: OSM way 27676178 (amenity=parking, 'Landslip Carpark', NT), polygon centroid
Notes: CORRECTION: it's paid (NT members free), not free; OSM's fee=no tag is out of date. Tier Small: about 1,300 m² in OSM, with no facilities.

Name: Ranmore West car park (National Trust)
Address: Ranmore Common Road, near Dorking RH5 6SY (NT walk page)
Description: A quiet, level gravel car park among the birch woods at the western end of Ranmore Common. It's the official start of the National Trust's walk to the Wotton Hatch pub.
Practical: National Trust car park; NT members free. The NT doesn't publish a separate tariff for Ranmore West, so check the signs on arrival (no phone signal). Gravel, with a level grass path to a picnic table. No toilets (nearest in Westcott). No overnight parking.
Nearby: Birch woodland of Ranmore Common straight from the car park, and the North Downs Way about 0.3 mile south. GHQ Line Pillboxes on the North Downs Way above Wotton and Ranmore (about 0.6 mile). Below the pillbox is 'God's seat', a bench with views over Dorking and Box Hill; local tradition gives two stories for the name. The NT's 5.3-mile circuit goes on to St John the Evangelist, Wotton and The Wotton Hatch (about 1.5 miles as the crow flies). St Barnabas Church, Ranmore is about 1.2 miles.
Coord_Source: OSM way 158903869 (amenity=parking, 'Ranmore Common (West)', NT), polygon centroid; matches NT walk start
Notes: CORRECTION: William listed it as main. It's the smaller of the two Ranmore NT car parks (OSM about 775 m² against Denbies Hillside's 2,000 m²), so it moves to Small.

Name: Friday Street car park
Address: Friday Street, Abinger Common RH5 6JR (Surrey County Council postcode)
Description: A free woodland car park above the tiny hamlet of Friday Street, with its much-photographed mill pond just down the lane. A lovely, shady start for the Tillingbourne valley and the long way up Leith Hill.
Practical: Free (Surrey County Council, on Wotton Estate land). Unmarked spaces; 1.9 m height barrier. No toilets. Information boards. A steep, narrow lane leads down to the hamlet. The Stephan Langton pub in the hamlet closed in 2020, so don't plan on lunch there.
Nearby: Friday Street Mill Pond (about 200 m down the lane). Woods of the NT's Severells Estate, Abinger Common and Wotton Common all around. Tillingbourne Waterfall (about 0.6 mile as the crow flies). The Abinger Hatch and St James Church in Abinger Common (about 0.75 mile on foot). Leith Hill Tower is about 2 miles south through the woods.
Notes: DUPLICATE: it appeared in both of William's files; merged into this one row. Tier Small: unpaved, about 1,800 m² in OSM, with no facilities. William's 40–60 spaces isn't published anywhere official.

Name: Broadmoor car park
Address: Sheephouse Lane, Broadmoor, Wotton RH5 6JY (Surrey County Council postcode)
Description: A free woodland car park in the quiet Broadmoor valley, between Friday Street and Leith Hill.
Practical: Free (Surrey County Council, on Wotton Estate land). Unmarked spaces; 1.9 m height barrier. No toilets.
Nearby: Woods of the NT's Severells Estate (about 0.2 mile). Friday Street Mill Pond (about 0.4 mile). Tillingbourne Waterfall (about 0.4 mile as the crow flies). Wotton Common and Abinger Common woods. Leith Hill Tower is about 1.5 miles south as the crow flies.
Coord_Source: OSM way 286958143 (amenity=parking, 'Broadmoor Car Park'), polygon centroid
Notes: Verified: SCC lists it as a free Leith Hill car park, not permit-only. Tier Small: about 1,800 m² in OSM, with no facilities.

Name: Abinger Roughs car park (National Trust)
Address: White Down Lane, Abinger Hammer RH5 6QS (nearest postcode, NT)
Description: A small, free National Trust car park on the Roughs, with flat, well-marked paths under 300-year-old oaks. A great one for little legs.
Practical: Free. Limited spaces, with accessible parking (NT). Unpaved. Dog bins. No toilets. It's half a mile up White Down Lane from the A25 at Crossways Farm.
Nearby: Samuel Wilberforce Memorial, marking where the bishop was killed in a riding fall in 1873 (about 100 m). The Witches' Broom Tree, a propped-up veteran beech on the NT tree trail (close by). Darwin walked these paths in the 1870s, the NT says. Blatchford Down chalk grassland is about 0.75 mile away. St John the Evangelist, Wotton and The Wotton Hatch are about 1 mile as the crow flies, and the Abinger Hammer clock about 1 mile.
Coord_Source: OSM way 103866290 (amenity=parking, 'Abinger Roughs', NT), polygon centroid
Notes: Verified: NT, free, not permit-only. Tier Small: the NT says 'limited parking' (OSM about 430 m²).

Name: White Down car park
Address: White Down Lane, Abinger RH5 6SL (Surrey County Council postcode)
Description: A free car park near the top of White Down Lane, for bluebell woods in spring, big views towards the Greensand Ridge and the North Downs Way.
Practical: Free (Surrey County Council, on Wotton Estate land). Unmarked spaces; gravel; 1.9 m height barrier. No toilets or bins. Nearest café and toilets: Gomshall Mill or the Compasses Inn (SCC).
Nearby: The North Downs Way runs just above the car park. GHQ Line Pillboxes on the North Downs Way above Wotton and Ranmore (about 0.4 mile). Blatchford Down (about 0.8 mile) and Hackhurst Downs (about 1 mile). SCC's Acorn trail (1.7 miles) and Butterfly trail (2 miles) start here. The Samuel Wilberforce Memorial and The Witches' Broom Tree on Abinger Roughs are about 1 mile.
Coord_Source: OSM way 60843777 (amenity=parking, 'White Down Car Park'), polygon centroid
Notes: CORRECTION: it's not NT. SCC says the site is owned by the Wotton Estate, with public access managed by SCC, and parking is free. Tier Small: OSM area about 1,400 m², with no facilities.

Name: Hurtwood Car Park 1, Holmbury Hill
Address: Near the top of Holmbury Hill, Holmbury St Mary (Friends of the Hurtwood car park 1)
Description: A free Hurtwood car park just below the summit of Holmbury Hill, one of the great Greensand Ridge viewpoints.
Practical: Free. The Friends of the Hurtwood ask for donations towards upkeep (foth.co.uk/donate). Gravel. No toilets. Popular with mountain bikers.
Nearby: Holmbury Hill summit (about 0.4 mile), with Iron Age hillfort earthworks and wide views south over the Weald. The open-access Hurtwood woods surround the car park. The King's Head and The Royal Oak in Holmbury St Mary are about 1–1.25 miles away, along with St Mary the Virgin, Holmbury St Mary. Pitch Hill is about 1.1 miles as the crow flies.
Coord_Source: OSM way 310410086 (amenity=parking, 'Hurtwood Car Park 1 - Holmbury Hill'), polygon centroid
Notes: Name corrected to the Friends of the Hurtwood's own numbering (Car Park 1). Tier Small: no facilities; OSM area about 1,900 m². OSM's capacity tag of 50 isn't official, so it's left out.

Name: Gomshall station car park
Description: A small, free station car park in the Tillingbourne valley. It's handy for a pub-to-pub stroll, or for walking up onto the Downs without the car.
Practical: 20 spaces including 3 Blue Badge, free, open 24 hours (GWR station information). Primarily for rail users, so please leave room for commuters on weekdays. No toilets at the station.
Nearby: Gomshall Mill and The Compasses Inn in Gomshall (about 0.25 mile). Tillingbourne Farm & Smokery (about 0.25 mile). The Abinger Hammer clock (about 0.5 mile) and Kingfisher Farm & Flower Shop (about 0.6 mile). Netley Park woods and their Type 24 Pillbox, and Little Kings Wood Viewpoint, are about 0.75–1 mile away. White Down is reached via Beggars Lane, per SCC.
Coord_Source: OSM way 197948214 (amenity=parking, beside Gomshall station), polygon centroid
Notes: Verified: real, free public station parking (GWR says 20 spaces). Tier Small.
